ety.text: From Middle English tyme, time, from Old English tīma (“time, period, space of time, season, lifetime, fixed time, favorable time, opportunity”), from Proto-West Germanic *tīmō, from Proto-Germanic *tīmô (“time”), from Proto-Indo-European *deh₂imō, from Proto-Indo-European *deh₂y- (“to divide”). Related to tide. Not related to Latin tempus.

senses.d: The inevitable progression into the future with the passing of present and past events.
ex: Time stops for nobody. the ebb and flow of time
Time is the fire in which we burn.

senses.d: The feeling of the passage of events and their relative duration, as experienced by an individual.
ex: Time flies when you're having fun.

senses.d: A dimension of spacetime with the opposite metric signature to space dimensions; the fourth dimension.
ex: Both science-fiction writers and physicists have written about travel through time.

senses.d: Change associated with the second law of thermodynamics; the physical and psychological result of increasing entropy.
ex: Time slows down when you approach the speed of light.
Eventually time would also die because no processes would continue, no light would flow.

senses.d: The property of a system which allows it to have more than one distinct configuration.
ex: An essential definition of time should entail neither speed nor direction, just change.

senses.d: A quantity of availability of duration.
ex: More time is needed to complete the project.
You had plenty of time, but you waited until the last minute.

senses.d: A measurement of a quantity of time; a numerical or general indication of a length of progression.
ex: a long time
Record the individual times for the processes in each batch.

senses.d: The serving of a prison sentence.
ex: The judge leniently granted a sentence with no hard time.
He is not living at home because he is doing time.

senses.d: An experience.
ex: We had a wonderful time at the party.

senses.d: An era; (articulated, sometimes in the plural) the current era, the current state of affairs.

senses.d: To measure or record the time, duration, or rate of something.
ex: I used a stopwatch to time myself running around the block.

senses.d: To choose when something commences or its duration.
